title: Onboarding pair: social proof ring and a notification permission with live preview
contains_third_party_content: Portrait photos, memoji-style avatars and an iOS lock-screen look.

observed.layout: Two phones with Dynamic Island on a pale background. Screen A: a ring of ten rounded-square portrait tiles of different sizes around a larger center portrait on a soft circular platter; 'Inspired people'; 'Number of people inspired by your game or completion.'; a black pill 'Cool!'. Screen B: a pink-lavender gradient with a nested phone showing a lock screen ('Monday, June 30 / 9:41') and two notification cards (Lia Maria, 'Added 23 photos to Outings.'; Tom Avril, 'Is eating at Done. Joondalup.') with small app badges on the avatars; emoji avatars float below; 'Don't miss out on what your friend's are up to.'; 'Never miss those precious moments.'; a black pill 'Turn on notifications'; a text link 'Another time'.
observed.hierarchy: Headline, then the visual, then the black pill.
observed.typography: Semibold sans headline; light grey body. Typeface unconfirmed.
observed.iconography: Rounded-square portrait tiles; memoji avatars; app badges.

implementation_notes: Avatar ring via polar positioning of tiles.
The permission screen is a soft ask shown before the system dialog.

concept_work.essence: Show what the permission will look like, offer a decline, keep one primary action.
what_makes_it_work: The preview gives the request a visible benefit.
A decline path ('Another time') is offered.
The black pill is identical on both screens.
The avatar ring turns a number into faces.
gaps_to_make_it_work: 'Cool!' is a vague label and 'your game or completion' is unclear.
Body copy on screen A measures about 2.62-2.83:1 and 'Another time' about 3.52-3.96:1.
The nested phone competes with the headline.

links: Both screens share the pill and type.
Screen B's preview ties to the permission it asks for.

pattern.name: Soft-ask permission screen with live preview
must_preserve: A preview of the real outcome
adaptation_examples: Location permission with a map preview.
Camera permission with a scanning preview.

lessons: Show the benefit before asking for a permission.

measured.palette_method: Median-cut quantization of the supplied image plus saturated-pixel hue medians. Approximate (JPEG). Items marked 'approx' were judged by eye.
measured.color_roles: White and pastel surfaces with one black pill as the only strong element.
measured.contrast_method: Estimated from compressed images. Background = dominant color in a box around the text. ratio_low = conservative estimate (mean of the most distant ~4% of pixels). ratio = best estimate (mean of the most distant ~1.5% of pixels; for text on a saturated background that appears near-white or near-black, the text is assumed pure white or black, because anti-aliasing of small text otherwise understates the contrast). Accessibility scores use ratio_low; critical failure CF1 uses ratio. Gradient or photo backgrounds are measured one text line at a time. Values within 0.4 of a threshold are borderline and should be verified in the source file.

evidence: Both screens have one obvious purpose and one action.
Airy composition, clear focal visuals and a single strong pill.
Onboarding conventions are followed (benefit, one primary, a decline) but the typo and vague labels weaken correctness.
Primary action and decline path are clear on both screens.
Pill, type and gradient are shared.
The live-preview permission screen is distinctive.
Scored on conservative values: primary text min 13.11:1; secondary text min 2.62:1; icon min n/a:1; non-color state cue: True.
accessibility.basis: computed from measured contrast + cue flag (scope: contrast and non-color cues only; touch targets, motion and screen-reader support cannot be assessed from a static image)

evaluation.readiness_key: A = ship with minor adjustments (>=80, no critical failure); B = needs specific fixes (60-79); C = rethink (<60)
evaluation.scope: Scored as presented in a static image. States, motion and behavior that are not shown are not scored as present.
